This marks the first initial prototype This basically takes a pollutino conc at the center and applies basic diffusion modelling to diffuse the pollution to all of the remaning matrix via basic diffusion modelling.

The V0.2 now includes a emission source defined as Industry(x, y, emission_rate, name=String) This gives the functionality of have an emission source at desired point in the map and then the advection apply_advection_current(ux,uy) thjs function applies the wind which are stored as constants in the file in the top Now the sim_run() function runs the simulations
Feel free to give it a try :)

The Problem: "Overshooting"Imagine a cell has 10 units of CO₂.If your D (Diffusion rate) is too high, the math might say: "Transfer 12 units to the neighbor."The cell now has -2 CO₂ (impossible physics).The neighbor has +12 CO₂.In the next step, the -2 tries to suck CO₂ back in, often overcompensating to +20.The simulation creates a feedback loop and explodes into infinity or random noise.The Solution: The "Speed Limit" MathYou don't have to guess. There is a rigid formula to calculate the maximum safe settings.For Diffusion: The logic cannot move more than 50% of a cell's contents in one step.$$D \le \frac{0.5}{(\Delta t / \Delta x^2)}$$(Since our grid distance $\Delta x$ is 1 pixel and time step $\Delta t$ is 1 tick, this simplifies to $D \le 0.25$).For Wind (Advection): The wind cannot move pollution across more than 1 cell in a single step.$$|Velocity| \le \frac{1.0}{(\Delta t / \Delta x)}$$(Simplifies to $|Wind| \le 1.0$).
I added a Stability Check system. Now, instead of guessing, the program calculates if your settings are mathematically safe before running.
I also added a Stack Height simulation as you requested earlier (simulated by a wider initial dispersion radius).

Version 0.4: City Infrastructure (Roads & Sinks)
Date: [Current Date] Goal: Model complex geometry (Roads) and negative emissions (Capture).
Methodology: Line Rasterization
To model roads on a discrete grid, we implemented a rasterization algorithm.
Logic: Used np.linspace to interpolate points between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
Sampling Rate: Determined by the Chebyshev distance (max(|dx|, |dy|)) to ensure 8-connected continuity (no gaps in the road).
Emissions: The total road emission rate is distributed evenly across all rasterized pixels to ensure conservation of mass.
Methodology: The Sink Term
Added the $S_{sink}$ term to the governing equation.
Constraint: Implemented max(0, current - removal) to prevent negative concentration (non-physical vacuum).
